slides.heading: How Brain-Computer Interfaces Work
slides.body: The technology turning thoughts into actions — and what it means for humanity

slides.heading: What Is a BCI?
slides.body: A Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) is a direct communication pathway between the brain and an external device. It reads electrical signals produced by neurons and translates them into commands a computer can understand — no muscles required.

slides.heading: How the Brain Signals Work
slides.body: Neurons communicate via tiny electrical impulses called action potentials. When you think about moving your hand, millions of neurons fire in coordinated patterns. BCIs detect these voltage changes — typically measured in microvolts — and decode the intent behind them.

slides.heading: Invasive vs. Non-Invasive BCIs
slides.body: Non-invasive BCIs (like EEG headsets) sit on the scalp and are safe but noisy. Invasive BCIs (like Utah arrays or Neuralink's threads) are implanted directly into brain tissue, capturing far cleaner signals with much higher resolution and speed.

slides.heading: Decoding Thoughts with AI
slides.body: Raw brain signals are meaningless without interpretation. Machine learning models are trained on thousands of signal samples to map patterns to intentions. The more data the model sees, the better it predicts whether you're thinking 'left,' 'right,' 'click,' or even composing a sentence.

slides.heading: Real-World Applications Today
slides.body: BCIs already help paralyzed patients type, control robotic arms, and even walk again via spinal stimulators. In 2024–2026, early adopters typed at 40+ words per minute using implanted devices — faster than many people type on a keyboard.

slides.heading: The Bidirectional Frontier
slides.body: Next-gen BCIs don't just read the brain — they write to it. Sensory feedback loops allow users to 'feel' a robotic hand gripping an object. This bidirectional communication opens the door to restoring lost senses and even augmenting healthy perception.

slides.heading: Key Challenges to Overcome
slides.body: Long-term implants face scar tissue buildup that degrades signal quality over months. Wireless data bandwidth limits real-time high-resolution readouts. And decoding complex abstract thoughts — not just motor commands — remains an unsolved scientific puzzle.

slides.heading: Ethics and Privacy Concerns
slides.body: Brain data is the most intimate data imaginable. Who owns your neural signals? Could employers or insurers demand access? Could governments use BCIs for surveillance? Researchers and policymakers are racing to establish 'neurorights' before the technology outpaces the law.

slides.heading: The Mind-Machine Merge Is Here
slides.body: BCIs are no longer science fiction — they are restoring function today and will redefine human capability tomorrow. Understanding this technology now means you're ready for the world it's building.
